quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is the correct way to make a right turn?

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move into the lane closest to the center line before turning.
Signal, slow down, and move into the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
Approach the corner in the right lane, but move toward the middle of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move into the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Use your signal to warn other drivers. Slow down and stay in the right lane, as close as possible to the right curb or edge of the road.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: At a flashing yellow light, slow down and proceed carefully. You do not have to stop completely.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your speed the same.
questions.explanation: When being passed, keep your speed steady. Do not speed up. Let the other vehicle pass safely and return to your lane.

questions.question: If a tire blows out, what should you do?

options.text: Press the brake and hold it.
Hold the steering wheel firmly and brake gently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly and brake gently.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel tightly and keep the car straight. Slow down gradually by easing off the gas and braking lightly. Pull off the road to a safe place.

questions.question: When driving in a construction zone, what should you do?

options.text: Expect construction workers to get out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for unexpected conditions.
questions.explanation: Construction zones have unpredictable conditions. Drive carefully and watch for hazards to protect yourself, other drivers, and construction workers.

questions.question: Which road surface freezes first?
questions.correctAnswerText: A bridge
questions.explanation: Bridges and overpasses freeze before other road surfaces. They also thaw out later. Ice can form on bridges even when nearby roads are dry.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of a road mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic moves in opposite directions. No one can pass from either direction.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on the highway, what should you do?

options.text: Park with all four wheels off the road if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park with all four wheels off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: When your vehicle breaks down, move it completely off the traveled road if you can.

questions.question: When it gets dark, what lights should you use so others can see you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your low beam headlights as daylight fades. Only use high beams in open areas with no other drivers nearby.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines between traffic lanes mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from the left.
Passing is allowed from the right.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid lines mean no one can pass from either direction.

questions.question: Which lane should you be in to make a left turn on a one-way street?

options.text: The lane closest to the left curb.
The lane closest to the center of the street.
The lane closest to the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: Always turn from the lane that is closest to the direction you want to go. For a left turn on a one-way street, use the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?

options.text: A curve in the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A curve in the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns you about a curve to the right.

questions.question: At what speed can hydroplaning start on wet roads?
questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when water builds up on the road. Most tires can push water away up to 35 mph. At speeds above 35 mph, tires cannot move the water fast enough and may lose grip on the road.

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, what must you do?

options.text: Yield to any traffic that is close enough to cause a collision.
Yield only to vehicles on your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any traffic that is close enough to cause a collision.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, you must let traffic in the road ahead go first. You can keep going if no other vehicles are coming. Be ready to stop.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog:

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading them across the street.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes. Give them the right-of-way in all situations.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You can turn right on a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turns allowed.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right. It is against the law to turn right where this sign is posted.

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Keep traffic away from dangerous work areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep traffic away from dangerous work areas.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for both workers and drivers. Look for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests. They warn you and show you where to go.

questions.question: If you are getting tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: On long trips, take a break every hour. If possible, share driving with another person so you can rest while they drive.

questions.question: Which statement about large trucks is true?

options.text: They need more distance to stop than passenger cars.
All large trucks have air brakes that stop them quickly.
They turn more easily than passenger cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need more distance to stop than passenger cars.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need much more space to stop. A passenger car going 55 mph stops in about 400 feet. A large truck at the same speed needs about 800 feet.

questions.question: When entering the interstate on a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, you should:

options.text: Go directly into the right lane and speed up to match traffic.
Use the shoulder to get up to traffic speed.
Speed up only after you find an open gap in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up only after you find an open gap in traffic.
questions.explanation: Wait for a gap in traffic, then speed up and enter. You should stay stopped while waiting for a safe gap to appear.

questions.question: The first thing that alcohol affects is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol reaches your brain and affects your judgment and skills first. These abilities are essential for safe driving.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:

options.text: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to all oncoming traffic. This includes bicycles and motorcycles.

questions.question: You should only drive at the maximum posted speed limit when:
questions.correctAnswerText: Conditions are good.
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest you can legally go under ideal conditions. Match the speed of other traffic and always drive safely. All drivers share this responsibility.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop (school buses, trucks carrying hazardous materials, etc.).

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings carefully. Cross only when no train is coming from either direction. Watch for vehicles that are required to stop at crossings, such as school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.

questions.question: Alcohol in any amount is:
questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is always a depressant. It slows your nerves and body functions. It makes you less careful and hurts your ability to focus and stay alert.
